kpis.query: For the latest run per subject (max started_at), compute passed / (cases - errored) case-weighted; program-level take the minimum across subjects where model is not null; a subject with cases-errored == 0 is reported no-signal.
kpis.reason: Every input is a stored field: passed, cases, errored give the scorable base and numerator; model distinguishes billed subjects; started_at orders runs; subject groups them.
kpis.caveat: eval-store is ok today (60 runs); a subject whose latest run predates the 7-day stale window is carried as stale via freshness, not re-read as current.

kpis.query: Over a trailing 4-week window: (sum(cost_usd) + store_plan_usd_per_month x window_days/30) / sum(cases - errored); also $ per sweep from the latest billed run of each subject.
kpis.proxy: The fixed-cost term uses the declared constant store_plan_usd_per_month rather than a Postgres billing feed, and the token x price recompute for absent cost cannot be done.
kpis.misses: The constant cannot see actual plan-price changes or overages, and there is no token count or price table to recompute a $0/absent cost_usd, so a run that fails to record cost renders as free rather than recomputed.
kpis.reason: cost_usd, cases, errored and started_at are stored; the store fixed cost is a declared constant, not a measured billing feed, which makes this a proxy per the rubric.
kpis.caveat: eval-store is ok today; spend_rows is 0, confirming there is no billing feed and the fixed term rests entirely on the constant.

kpis.reason: Requires GitHub release tags per subject to compare against the latest run's code_version; not_available lists GitHub commits, tags, releases and PRs as absent. The catalog carries eval-store.code_version but nothing to compare it against, so newer-than-measured versions cannot be counted. To re-instrument, collect per-repo release tags (with a tag-to-version mapping) for the six subjects.

kpis.query: From the latest run per subject (max started_at): errored / cases x 100; a run with cases == 0 is no-signal; program-level take the maximum with the subject named.
kpis.reason: errored and cases are stored counts; subject and started_at select the latest run per subject.
kpis.caveat: eval-store is ok today (60 runs); reflects only the last recorded run per subject, which may be stale relative to the subject's freshness.

kpis.query: Over the trailing 4 weeks, group runs by (subject, model) where model is not null; mean(cost_usd) per group, shown with mean/total case count; deterministic (null model) runs excluded.
kpis.reason: cost_usd, cases, subject, model and started_at are all stored fields; grouping and windowing use them directly.
kpis.caveat: eval-store is ok today; a run whose consumer failed to set cost_usd records 0.0 and would understate a group's mean, and there is no price table to detect it (a $0 run is a broken instrument, not free).

notes: unmeasured-code-versions was adopted pending source verification in RC1-303 (per the tree's own adoption note) and fails here: the GitHub feed it needs (release tags, versions) is explicitly not_available, and eval-store carries only code_version with nothing to compare it to.

cost-per-verified-case and cost-per-run-by-model both depend on cost_usd, which the catalog notes can be 0.0 when a consumer does not set it; with no token counts or price table stored, the definitions' 'recompute from tokens x price' fallback cannot be executed \

spThe store fixed-cost term relies on the constant store_plan_usd_per_month (5.0) rather than a billing feed; spend_rows is 0 in today's snapshot, confirming no Postgres billing feed exists, so cost-per-verified-case is a proxy rather than confirmed.

Several rejected candidates (regressions caught before merge, judge/human agreement) correctly lean on absent records \u2014 no branch/PR feed and no per-case judge rows exist in the catalog, consistent with not_available.
